authors: Heydar Soudani; Hamed Zamani; Faegheh Hasibi
suggested_section: Calibration and Control / Uncertainty in RAG
why_relevant: Proposes a UQ method for retrieval-augmented reasoning that captures uncertainty from both retriever and generator, and applies it to abstention and model selection—directly relevant to calibration/control and uncertainty under unreliable evidence.

title: Parameters vs. Context: Fine-Grained Control of Knowledge Reliance in Language Models
authors: Baolong Bi; Shenghua Liu; Yiwei Wang; Yilong Xu; Junfeng Fang; Lingrui Mei; Xueqi Cheng
why_relevant: Proposes CK-PLUG, a decoding-time method to control LLM reliance on parametric vs retrieved knowledge using entropy-based confidence gain to detect conflicts, directly addressing knowledge conflict and calibration/control in RAG.

title: Divide-Then-Align: Honest Alignment based on the Knowledge Boundary of RAG
authors: Xin Sun; Jianan Xie; Zhongqi Chen; Qiang Liu; Shu Wu; Yuehe Chen; Bowen Song; Weiqiang Wang; Zilei Wang; Liang Wang
why_relevant: Proposes DPO-based alignment for RAG to abstain ('I don't know') when queries fall outside both parametric and retrieval knowledge boundaries, directly addressing calibration, abstention, and noisy retrieval robustness.

title: ATM: Adversarial Tuning Multi-agent System Makes a Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generator
why_relevant: ATM proposes adversarial multi-agent tuning to make RAG generators robust against fabricated/noisy retrieved documents, directly addressing robustness under unreliable evidence.

title: Understanding Data Poisoning Attacks for RAG: Insights and Algorithms
why_relevant: Proposes both a new defense (DRS) and stealthier attack against data poisoning of RAG retrieval corpora, directly addressing adversarial corruption robustness.

title: When Evidence Conflicts: Uncertainty and Order Effects in Retrieval-Augmented Biomedical Question Answering
authors: Yikun Han; Mengfei Lan; Halil Kilicoglu
why_relevant: Studies RAG under conflicting biomedical evidence, examining order effects, calibration, and proposing a conflict-aware abstention score. Directly addresses knowledge conflict, uncertainty, and selective prediction.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (biomedical) and uses an existing benchmark.

title: The Synthetic Web: Adversarially-Curated Mini-Internets for Diagnosing Epistemic Weaknesses of Language Agents
authors: Shrey Shah; Levent Ozgur
why_relevant: Introduces a controlled benchmark for evaluating web agents/RAG under adversarial ranking with misinformation, measuring accuracy collapse, search escalation, and miscalibration—directly relevant to robustness, conflict, and calibration themes.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on web agents rather than pure RAG pipelines, but threat model and findings transfer.

title: Seeing through the Conflict: Transparent Knowledge Conflict Handling in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Hua Ye; Siyuan Chen; Ziqi Zhong; Canran Xiao; Haoliang Zhang; Yuhan Wu; Fei Shen
why_relevant: Proposes a framework for detecting and resolving context-memory conflicts in RAG via interpretable signals (semantic match, factual consistency, self-answerability), directly addressing knowledge conflict and confidence-aware control.

title: MEMSAD: Gradient-Coupled Anomaly Detection for Memory Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Agents
authors: Ishrith Gowda
why_relevant: Formalizes memory poisoning attacks on retrieval-augmented agents as a Stackelberg game and proposes MEMSAD, a calibration-based anomaly detection defense with certified detection radius and minimax optimality guarantees. Directly addresses adversarial corruption of RAG memory and calibration-based defenses.

title: LLM-Oriented Information Retrieval: A Denoising-First Perspective
authors: Lu Dai; Liang Sun; Fanpu Cao; Ziyang Rao; Cehao Yang; Hao Liu; Hui Xiong
why_relevant: A perspective/survey paper on denoising across the RAG pipeline, covering noise sensitivity, prompt injection, verifiability, and context engineering—directly aligned with the survey's scope.

title: Is Conformal Factuality for RAG-based LLMs Robust? Novel Metrics and Systematic Insights
authors: Yi Chen; Daiwei Chen; Sukrut Madhav Chikodikar; Caitlyn Heqi Yin; Ramya Korlakai Vinayak
why_relevant: Systematically evaluates conformal factuality filtering for RAG, showing fragility under distribution shifts and distractors, and proposes informativeness-aware metrics—directly addressing calibration, robustness, and evaluation of RAG under unreliable evidence.

title: GRACE: Reinforcement Learning for Grounded Response and Abstention under Contextual Evidence
authors: Yibo Zhao; Jiapeng Zhu; Zichen Ding; Xiang Li
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: Abstention and Grounding
why_relevant: GRACE is an RL framework that jointly trains an RAG model to ground answers in evidence and abstain when retrieved context is insufficient, directly addressing calibration/abstention and unreliable evidence handling.

title: Exploring Knowledge Conflicts for Faithful LLM Reasoning: Benchmark and Method
authors: Tianzhe Zhao; Jiaoyan Chen; Shuxiu Zhang; Haiping Zhu; Qika Lin; Jun Liu
why_relevant: Introduces ConflictQA, a benchmark for cross-source knowledge conflicts (text vs KG) in RAG, plus an explanation-based method (XoT) to mitigate evidence bias. Directly addresses knowledge conflict and evaluation under unreliable evidence.

title: ERA: Evidence-based Reliability Alignment for Honest Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Sunguk Shin; Meeyoung Cha; Byung-Jun Lee; Sungwon Park
suggested_section: Calibration and Abstention under Knowledge Conflict
why_relevant: ERA directly addresses knowledge conflict between parametric and retrieved evidence, uses evidential deep learning and Dempster-Shafer theory to calibrate confidence, and enables abstention under unsupported queries — central themes of the survey.

title: Cordon-MAS: Defending RAG against Knowledge Poisoning via Information-Flow Control
authors: Zhe Yu; Wenpeng Xing; Gaolei Li; Shuguang Xiong; Hongzhi Wang; Xuyang Teng; Meng Han
why_relevant: Proposes an architectural multi-agent defense against RAG knowledge poisoning, framing it as an information-flow control problem and showing a monitoring-control gap in LLMs handling poisoned evidence.

title: Beyond Explicit Refusals: Soft-Failure Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Wentao Zhang; Yan Zhuang; ZhuHang Zheng; Mingfei Zhang; Jiawen Deng; Fuji Ren
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Jamming Attacks
why_relevant: Proposes a novel soft-failure jamming attack on RAG via adversarial document injection, exploiting safety alignment to induce non-informative answers while evading detection. Directly relevant to adversarial corruption and availability threats in RAG.

title: Architecture Matters: Comparing RAG Systems under Knowledge Base Poisoning
authors: Samuel Korn
why_relevant: Evaluates four RAG architectures against adversarial knowledge base poisoning under N=1 settings, decomposing retrieval- vs generation-stage vulnerabilities and introducing a behavioral taxonomy capturing contradiction detection and hedging.

title: ArbGraph: Conflict-Aware Evidence Arbitration for Reliable Long-Form Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Qingying Niu; Yuhao Wang; Ruiyang Ren; Bohui Fang; Wayne Xin Zhao
why_relevant: ArbGraph directly addresses conflict resolution and noise suppression in RAG by arbitrating evidence credibility through a conflict-aware graph before generation, targeting retrieved-vs-retrieved conflicts and noisy long-form RAG.

title: Resisting Contextual Interference in RAG via Parametric-Knowledge Reinforcement
authors: Chenyu Lin; Yilin Wen; Du Su; Hexiang Tan; Fei Sun; Muhan Chen; Chenfu Bao; Zhonghou Lyu
why_relevant: Proposes an RL framework (Knowledgeable-R1) that trains LLMs to balance parametric vs contextual knowledge, resisting misleading/counterfactual retrieved context. Directly addresses knowledge conflict and robustness to noisy retrieval.

title: EcoSafeRAG: Efficient Security through Context Analysis in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Ruobing Yao; Yifei Zhang; Shuang Song; Neng Gao; Chenyang Tu
why_relevant: Proposes a defense framework against RAG poisoning, prompt injection, and adversarial document attacks via sentence-level segmentation and bait-guided context diversity detection, without relying on LLM internal knowledge.

title: Disabling Self-Correction in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Stealthy Retriever Poisoning
authors: Yanbo Dai; Zhenlan Ji; Zongjie Li; Kuan Li; Shuai Wang
why_relevant: Introduces a novel retriever-poisoning attack that suppresses LLM self-correction ability, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and context-vs-parametric conflict robustness in RAG.

title: CtrlRAG: Black-box Document Poisoning Attacks for Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
authors: Runqi Sui
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning Attacks and Defenses
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box document poisoning attack against RAG and a defense based on parametric/non-parametric memory confrontation, directly addressing adversarial corruption and conflict-based defense.

title: Conflict-Aware Soft Prompting for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Eunseong Choi; June Park; Hyeri Lee; Jongwuk Lee
why_relevant: Proposes CARE, a conflict-aware soft prompting method that helps RAG resolve context-memory conflicts via grounded/adversarial training, directly addressing knowledge conflict and reliability of retrieved evidence.

title: Bounding Hallucinations: Information-Theoretic Guarantees for RAG Systems via Merlin-Arthur Protocols
authors: Björn Deiseroth; Max Henning Höth; Kristian Kersting; Letitia Parcalabescu
why_relevant: Proposes a training framework with adversarial (Morgana) and helpful (Merlin) provers to make RAG generators abstain on insufficient evidence, resist misleading context, and ground in causal evidence, with information-theoretic guarantees. Directly targets hallucination, reject behavior, and robustness to adversarial/noisy context.

title: Beyond Black-Box Interventions: Latent Probing for Faithful Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Linfeng Gao; Qinggang Zhang; Baolong Bi; Bo Zeng; Zheng Yuan; Zerui Chen; Zhimin Wei; Shenghua Liu; Linlong Xu; Longyue Wang; Weihua Luo; Jinsong Su
why_relevant: Proposes ProbeRAG, using latent-space probing to detect knowledge conflicts and filter noisy context, directly addressing faithfulness under unreliable evidence.

title: Synchronous Faithfulness Monitoring for Trustworthy Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Di Wu; Jia-Chen Gu; Fan Yin; Nanyun Peng; Kai-Wei Chang
why_relevant: Proposes a synchronous faithfulness monitor (SynCheck) and faithfulness-oriented decoding to detect and prevent unfaithful RAG outputs, directly addressing context compliance, calibration/abstention, and decoding-time control under unreliable evidence.

title: [] On the Vulnerability of Applying Retrieval-Augmented Generation within Knowledge-Intensive Application Domains
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption: poisoning attacks and defenses
why_relevant: Proposes universal poisoning attacks against RAG retrieval systems in knowledge-intensive domains and a detection-based defense, directly addressing adversarial corruption of retrieval.

title: Revisiting Robust RAG: Do We Still Need Complex Robust Training in the Era of Powerful LLMs?
why_relevant: Analyzes robust RAG training methods (RetRobust, RAAT, ATM) against retrieval noise across model scales, examining confidence calibration and attention patterns, directly relevant to noise robustness and calibration discussions.

title: After Retrieval, Before Generation: Enhancing the Trustworthiness of Large Language Models in RAG
why_relevant: Proposes BRIDGE framework and TRD benchmark explicitly addressing parametric vs retrieved knowledge conflicts, poisoned context, outdated knowledge, and abstention—directly aligning with conflict, calibration/control, and evaluation themes.

title: SURE-RAG: Sufficiency and Uncertainty-Aware Evidence Verification for Selective Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jingxi Qiu; Zeyu Han; Cheng Huang
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: Abstention and Selective RAG
why_relevant: SURE-RAG directly addresses evidence sufficiency verification, selective answering/abstention, and uncertainty/conflict signals in RAG, with an artifact-aware evaluation protocol. This aligns with the survey's calibration/control and unreliable-evidence themes.
why_not_or_caveat: Benchmark is constructed (HotpotQA-RAG v3); generalization beyond multi-hop QA is limited.

title: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Medical Multi-Modal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Peiru Yang; Haoran Zheng; Tong Ju; Shiting Wang; Wanchun Ni; Jiajun Liu; Shangguang Wang; Yongfeng Huang; Tao Qi
why_relevant: Proposes a query-agnostic knowledge poisoning attack on medical multimodal RAG, targeting both retrieval hijacking and generation manipulation, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (medical multimodal); attack-only, no defense.

title: BalanceRAG: Joint Risk Calibration for Cascaded Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zijun Jia; Yuanchang Ye; Sen Jia; Yiyao Qian; Haoning Wang; Baojie Chen; Diyin Tang; Jinsong Yu; Zhiyuan Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a finite-sample risk-controlled calibration method for cascaded LLM-only/RAG routing with abstention, directly addressing when to retrieve and when to abstain under uncertainty.

title: [] The Silent Saboteur: Imperceptible Adversarial Attacks against Black-Box Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Retrieval and Poisoning Attacks
why_relevant: Proposes an imperceptible black-box adversarial attack against RAG that perturbs a target document to enter top-k retrieval and steer LLM answers, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and retrieval attacks.
why_not_or_caveat: Attack-only; no defense or calibration contribution.

title: [] The RAG Paradox: A Black-Box Attack Exploiting Unintentional Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
why_relevant: Proposes a realistic black-box corpus poisoning attack on RAG systems that exploits source disclosure, producing natural-looking poisoned documents that degrade RAG performance.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses solely on attack methodology; no defense or calibration component.

title: Who Taught the Lie? Responsibility Attribution for Poisoned Knowledge in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Baolei Zhang; Haoran Xin; Yuxi Chen; Zhuqing Liu; Biao Yi; Tong Li; Lihai Nie; Zheli Liu; Minghong Fang
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box responsibility attribution framework to identify poisoned texts in RAG knowledge bases, directly addressing adversarial corruption and forensics under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on post-hoc attribution rather than prevention or calibration; narrower than general robustness.

title: Topic-FlipRAG: Topic-Orientated Adversarial Opinion Manipulation Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation Models
authors: Yuyang Gong; Zhuo Chen; Jiawei Liu; Miaokun Chen; Fengchang Yu; Wei Lu; Xiaofeng Wang; Xiaozhong Liu
why_relevant: Proposes a topic-level opinion manipulation poisoning attack against RAG and evaluates existing defenses (perplexity, reranking, paraphrasing), directly relevant to adversarial corruption and defense robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused narrowly on opinion manipulation rather than general robustness.

title: Resolving Conflicting Evidence in Automated Fact-Checking: A Study on Retrieval-Augmented LLMs
authors: Ziyu Ge; Yuhao Wu; Daniel Wai Kit Chin; Roy Ka-Wei Lee; Rui Cao
why_relevant: Introduces CONFACT, a dataset and evaluation of RAG models facing conflicting retrieved evidence from sources of varying credibility, directly studying retrieved-vs-retrieved conflict and proposing credibility-aware mitigation.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to fact-checking, but conflict-handling findings generalize.

title: RAG-Pull: Turning Retrieval into a Code-Injection Channel via Invisible Unicode Perturbations
authors: Aritra Dhar; Vasilije Stambolic; Lukas Cavigelli
why_relevant: Introduces a black-box attack on RAG pipelines using invisible Unicode perturbations to redirect retrieval toward malicious code, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on code-generation RAG specifically.

title: Poisoned-MRAG: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks to Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Yinuo Liu; Zenghui Yuan; Guiyao Tie; Jiawen Shi; Pan Zhou; Lichao Sun; Neil Zhenqiang Gong
why_relevant: Introduces the first knowledge poisoning attack on multimodal RAG, with cross-modal dirty- and clean-label strategies, and evaluates four defenses, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal/VLM setting; less directly applicable to text-only RAG.

title: One Pic is All it Takes: Poisoning Visual Document Retrieval Augmented Generation with a Single Image
authors: Ezzeldin Shereen; Dan Ristea; Shae McFadden; Burak Hasircioglu; Vasilios Mavroudis; Chris Hicks
why_relevant: Demonstrates poisoning attacks against visual document RAG via a single adversarial image, addressing both retrieval and generation conditions in white- and black-box settings. Extends KB poisoning threat models to multimodal RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on visual modality; limited defense exploration.

title: FlippedRAG: Black-Box Opinion Manipulation Adversarial Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation Models
authors: Zhuo Chen; Yuyang Gong; Jiawei Liu; Miaokun Chen; Haotan Liu; Qikai Cheng; Fan Zhang; Wei Lu; Xiaozhong Liu
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box poisoning attack against RAG retrievers for opinion manipulation on controversial topics, and evaluates defenses, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on opinion manipulation rather than factual poisoning; defenses analysis is limited.

title: Faithfulness-Aware Uncertainty Quantification for Fact-Checking the Output of Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Ekaterina Fadeeva; Aleksandr Rubashevskii; Dzianis Piatrashyn; Roman Vashurin; Shehzaad Dhuliawala; Artem Shelmanov; Timothy Baldwin; Preslav Nakov; Mrinmaya Sachan; Maxim Panov
why_relevant: Proposes FRANQ, a faithfulness-aware uncertainty quantification method to detect factual errors in RAG outputs, distinguishing between hallucinations from retrieval grounding vs. parametric knowledge. Directly relevant to calibration and conflict between parametric and retrieved knowledge.

title: Defending against Indirect Prompt Injection by Instruction Detection
authors: Tongyu Wen; Chenglong Wang; Xiyuan Yang; Haoyu Tang; Yueqi Xie; Lingjuan Lyu; Zhicheng Dou; Fangzhao Wu
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Defenses against Indirect Prompt Injection
why_relevant: Proposes a detection-based defense against indirect prompt injection in RAG using LLM hidden states/gradients, directly addressing adversarial corruption of retrieved content.

title: DeRAG: Black-box Adversarial Attacks on Multiple Retrieval-Augmented Generation Applications via Prompt Injection
authors: Jerry Wang; Fang Yu
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box differential evolution attack that injects adversarial suffixes to manipulate RAG retrieval rankings, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses solely on attack methodology without defense or calibration discussion.

title: CtrlA: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Inherent Control
authors: Liu Huanshuo; Hao Zhang; Zhijiang Guo; Jing Wang; Kuicai Dong; Xiangyang Li; Yi Quan Lee; Cong Zhang; Yong Liu
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: CtrlA addresses when to retrieve in adaptive RAG via honesty steering and confidence monitoring from internal representations, directly relevant to calibration/control over retrieval triggering.

title: ConfRAG: Confidence-Guided Retrieval-Augmenting Generation
authors: Yin Huang; Yifan Ethan Xu; Kai Sun; Vera Yan; Alicia Sun; Haidar Khan; Jimmy Nguyen; Jingxiang Chen; Mohammad Kachuee; Zhaojiang Lin; Yue Liu; Aaron Colak; Anuj Kumar; Wen-tau Yih; Xin Luna Dong
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve and Abstain
why_relevant: Proposes confidence-calibrated fine-tuning (ConfQA) to abstain with 'I am unsure' and use this signal to trigger RAG only when needed, directly addressing when-to-retrieve and abstention/calibration.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on triggering and hallucination suppression; does not address adversarial or conflict robustness.

title: Chain-of-Thought Poisoning Attacks against R1-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Hongru Song; Yu-an Liu; Ruqing Zhang; Jiafeng Guo; Yixing Fan
why_relevant: Proposes a novel knowledge base poisoning attack targeting R1-based reasoning RAG systems by wrapping erroneous knowledge in chain-of-thought templates, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Narrow focus on attack against R1-based systems; no defense proposed.

title: Who's Who: Large Language Models Meet Knowledge Conflicts in Practice
authors: Quang Hieu Pham; Hoang Ngo; Anh Tuan Luu; Dat Quoc Nguyen
why_relevant: Introduces WhoQA, a benchmark for evaluating LLM behavior under retrieved-vs-retrieved knowledge conflicts arising from same-name entities, directly relevant to the conflict and evaluation sections.

title: Unanswerability Evaluation for Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Xiangyu Peng; Prafulla Kumar Choubey; Caiming Xiong; Chien-Sheng Wu
suggested_section: Evaluation benchmarks for abstention and unanswerability
why_relevant: Introduces UAEval4RAG, a benchmark for evaluating RAG systems' ability to reject six categories of unanswerable queries (underspecified, false-presupposition, nonsensical, modality-limited, safety, OOD), directly relevant to abstention, OOD, and evaluation under unreliable evidence.

title: Studying Large Language Model Behaviors Under Context-Memory Conflicts With Real Documents
authors: Evgenii Kortukov; Alexander Rubinstein; Elisa Nguyen; Seong Joon Oh
why_relevant: Analyzes context-memory knowledge conflicts in RAG using real documents, identifying a parametric bias that hinders knowledge updating. Directly relevant to the survey's knowledge conflict section.

title: RetrievalQA: Assessing Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Short-form Open-Domain Question Answering
authors: Zihan Zhang; Meng Fang; Ling Chen
suggested_section: Calibration and control: when to retrieve
why_relevant: Introduces RetrievalQA benchmark and TA-ARE method for adaptive retrieval, evaluating when LLMs should trigger retrieval—directly relevant to calibration/control over when to retrieve.

title: Rag and Roll: An End-to-End Evaluation of Indirect Prompt Manipulations in LLM-based Application Frameworks
authors: Gianluca De Stefano; Lea Schönherr; Giancarlo Pellegrino
why_relevant: End-to-end evaluation of indirect prompt injection attacks against RAG pipelines, examining how configuration choices affect attack success—directly relevant to adversarial corruption and robustness evaluation.

title: RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG
authors: Tianjun Zhang; Shishir G. Patil; Naman Jain; Sheng Shen; Matei Zaharia; Ion Stoica; Joseph E. Gonzalez
why_relevant: RAFT fine-tunes LLMs with distractor documents to make them robust against irrelevant/noisy retrieved context, directly addressing distraction and noisy retrieval in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on domain-specific adaptation rather than broad robustness taxonomy.

title: Poisoned LangChain: Jailbreak LLMs by LangChain
authors: Ziqiu Wang; Jun Liu; Shengkai Zhang; Yang Yang
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Indirect Prompt Injection
why_relevant: Proposes an indirect jailbreak attack via poisoning the external knowledge base used by LangChain RAG, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused narrowly on Chinese LLM jailbreak via RAG poisoning; no defense analysis.

title: Neural Exec: Learning (and Learning from) Execution Triggers for Prompt Injection Attacks
authors: Dario Pasquini; Martin Strohmeier; Carmela Troncoso
why_relevant: Introduces learned prompt-injection triggers designed to survive RAG preprocessing (chunking, filtering), demonstrating a novel indirect injection attack against RAG pipelines.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on attack methodology; does not propose defenses or calibration.

title: Cutting Off the Head Ends the Conflict: A Mechanism for Interpreting and Mitigating Knowledge Conflicts in Language Models
authors: Zhuoran Jin; Pengfei Cao; Hongbang Yuan; Yubo Chen; Jiexin Xu; Huaijun Li; Xiaojian Jiang; Kang Liu; Jun Zhao
why_relevant: Interprets the mechanism of knowledge conflicts between parametric memory and external context, and proposes attention-head pruning to control whether LMs follow internal memory or retrieved context—directly relevant to the conflict and control axes of the survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on mechanistic interpretability on a controlled factual recall task rather than full RAG pipelines.

title: Backdoored Retrievers for Prompt Injection Attacks on Retrieval Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
authors: Cody Clop; Yannick Teglia
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Retriever Backdoors and Prompt Injection
why_relevant: Proposes backdoor attack on dense retriever and corpus poisoning for prompt injection in RAG, expanding attack objectives beyond misinformation (malicious links, ads, DoS).
why_not_or_caveat: Limited scope; small-scale empirical study.

title: [] Tricking Retrievers with Influential Tokens: An Efficient Black-Box Corpus Poisoning Attack
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box corpus poisoning attack (DIGA) against RAG retrievers, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Attack-only; no defense or calibration contribution.

title: [] Token-Level Precise Attack on RAG: Searching for the Best Alternatives to Mislead Generation
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption / Poisoning Attacks on RAG
why_relevant: Proposes a token-level attack on RAG that jointly targets retrieval and generation, injecting malicious passages into the knowledge base to mislead the reader. Directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Attack-only; no defense or calibration contribution.

title: [] RIPRAG: Hack a Black-box Retrieval-Augmented Generation Question-Answering System with Reinforcement Learning
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box RL-based poisoning attack against RAG systems, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption axis of the survey.

title: [] RAG Safety: Exploring Knowledge Poisoning Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
why_relevant: First systematic study of data poisoning attacks against KG-based RAG, injecting perturbation triples to mislead multi-hop reasoning; analyzes retrieval vs generation stage vulnerabilities and LLM robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses specifically on KG-RAG rather than text-based RAG.

title: [] One shot dominance: Knowledge poisoning attack on retrieval-augmented generation systems
why_relevant: Proposes AuthChain, a single-document knowledge poisoning attack on RAG that exploits retrieval ranking and overcomes LLM internal-knowledge bias via authority signals, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and knowledge conflict.

title: [] MM-PoisonRAG: Disrupting Multimodal RAG with Local and Global Poisoning Attacks
why_relevant: Proposes localized and globalized knowledge poisoning attacks against multimodal RAG, evaluates across retrievers/MLLMs, and tests defenses—directly relevant to adversarial corruption in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal RAG poisoning specifically; less central to text-only RAG robustness.

title: [] Hoist with His Own Petard: Inducing Guardrails to Facilitate Denial-of-Service Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation of LLMs
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Injection Attacks
why_relevant: Proposes MutedRAG, a denial-of-service poisoning attack that injects jailbreak prompts into the knowledge base to trigger LLM guardrails, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.

title: [] A Few Words Can Distort Graphs: Knowledge Poisoning Attacks on Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
why_relevant: Proposes knowledge poisoning attacks on GraphRAG via minimal text edits, showing defenses fail; directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG knowledge bases.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on GraphRAG variant rather than standard RAG.

title: Traceback of Poisoned Texts in Poisoning Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation
why_relevant: Proposes RAGForensics, a post-hoc traceback system to identify poisoned texts in RAG knowledge databases, directly addressing adversarial corruption defense.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on forensic traceback rather than inference-time robustness; complementary to mainstream defenses.

title: RevPRAG: Revealing Poisoning Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation through LLM Activation Analysis
why_relevant: RevPRAG detects RAG poisoning attacks via LLM activation analysis, directly addressing adversarial corruption defenses in RAG.

title: Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Large Language Models
why_relevant: Proposes an evaluation framework and instruction-based methods for LLMs to detect, localize, and respond to parametric-vs-contextual knowledge conflicts, directly relevant to the conflict and calibration sections.
why_not_or_caveat: Uses synthetic conflicts rather than real retrieval pipelines.

title: Beyond RAG vs. Long-Context: Learning Distraction-Aware Retrieval for Efficient Knowledge Grounding
authors: Seongwoong Shim; Myunsoo Kim; Jae Hyeon Cho; Byung-Jun Lee
why_relevant: Proposes a distraction-aware retrieval method that explicitly balances information coverage against distraction from irrelevant passages, directly addressing noisy retrieval and LLM distraction in RAG.

title: Whose Facts Win? LLM Source Preferences under Knowledge Conflicts
authors: Jakob Schuster; Vagrant Gautam; Katja Markert
why_relevant: Studies inter-context knowledge conflicts in RAG, examining how LLMs resolve conflicting evidence based on source credibility and revealing repetition-based vulnerabilities akin to disinformation attacks. Proposes a fine-tuning mitigation.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on source credibility dimension rather than the full breadth of RAG robustness.

title: Towards Unsupervised Adversarial Document Detection in Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Patrick Levi
why_relevant: Proposes an unsupervised detector for adversarial/poisoned context documents in RAG using activations, embeddings, and entropy-based uncertainty, directly addressing defense against retrieval poisoning.
why_not_or_caveat: Preliminary study with limited scale (100 HotpotQA questions, simple Grubb's test).

title: Towards Secure Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Review of Threats, Defenses and Benchmarks
authors: Yanming Mu; Hao Hu; Feiyang Li; Qiao Yuan; Jiang Wu; Zichuan Liu; Pengcheng Liu; Mei Wang; Hongwei Zhou; Yuling Liu
why_relevant: End-to-end survey of RAG security threats (poisoning, adversarial, membership inference), defenses, and benchmarks, directly overlapping with the adversarial corruption and evaluation sections of the target survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on security/privacy rather than broader robustness aspects like distraction, calibration, or knowledge conflict.

title: Towards Dependable Retrieval-Augmented Generation Using Factual Confidence Prediction
authors: Florian Geissler; Francesco Carella; Laura Fieback; Jakob Spiegelberg
why_relevant: Proposes conformal prediction-based retrieval filtering and attention-based hallucination/factuality classification to certify RAG outputs, directly addressing calibration, retrieval trust, and detecting unsupported answers.

title: The Curse of Helpfulness: Inverse Scaling Law in Robustness to Distractor Instructions via DistractionIF
authors: Zeli Su; Zhankai Xu; Tianlei Chen; Longfei Zheng; Xiaolu Zhang; Jun Zhou; Wentao Zhang
why_relevant: Introduces DistractionIF benchmark measuring LLM robustness to instruction-like distractor noise in reference text for RAG/agent settings, revealing inverse scaling and proposing RL-based mitigation.

title: RefineRAG: Word-Level Poisoning Attacks via Retriever-Guided Text Refinement
authors: Ziye Wang; Guanyu Wang; Kailong Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a stealthy word-level poisoning attack against RAG retrievers, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption section of the survey.

why_relevant: Proposes a defense against indirect prompt injection attacks in RAG contexts, directly addressing adversarial corruption of retrieved evidence.

title: PIDP-Attack: Combining Prompt Injection with Database Poisoning Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Haozhen Wang; Haoyue Liu; Jionghao Zhu; Zhichao Wang; Yongxin Guo; Xiaoying Tang
why_relevant: Proposes a compound attack combining prompt injection and database poisoning against RAG, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.

title: Neuro-RIT: Neuron-Guided Instruction Tuning for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Language Model
authors: Jaemin Kim; Jae O Lee; Sumyeong Ahn; Seo Yeon Park
why_relevant: Proposes a neuron-guided instruction tuning method to make RALMs robust to noisy/irrelevant retrieved contexts, directly addressing the noisy retrieval and distraction robustness theme.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on a specific tuning technique rather than broad analysis or benchmark.

title: MTRAG-UN: A Benchmark for Open Challenges in Multi-Turn RAG Conversations
authors: Sara Rosenthal; Yannis Katsis; Vraj Shah; Lihong He; Lucian Popa; Marina Danilevsky
suggested_section: Evaluation/benchmarks for OOD, abstention, and clarification
why_relevant: MTRAG-UN benchmarks multi-turn RAG on unanswerable, underspecified, non-standalone questions and unclear responses, directly probing abstention, clarification, and handling of ambiguous/unsupported queries.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on multi-turn conversational challenges rather than adversarial or noisy retrieval per se.

title: MPIB: A Benchmark for Medical Prompt Injection Attacks and Clinical Safety in LLMs
authors: Junhyeok Lee; Han Jang; Kyu Sung Choi

why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark for direct and indirect (RAG-mediated) prompt injection in clinical settings, with outcome-based metrics distinguishing instruction compliance from downstream harm. Directly relevant to adversarial corruption and evaluation of robust RAG.

title: Lost in the Evidence? Reproducing Document Position and Context Size Effects in RAG
authors: Jorge Gabín; Anxo Perez; Javier Parapar
why_relevant: Systematic reproducibility study of position bias (lost-in-the-middle) and context size effects in RAG under imperfect retrieval, directly addressing robustness to noisy/ordered evidence and evaluation methodology.

title: LogicPoison: Logical Attacks on Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Yilin Xiao; Jin Chen; Qinggang Zhang; Yujing Zhang; Chuang Zhou; Longhao Yang; Lingfei Ren; Xin Yang; Xiao Huang
why_relevant: Proposes a novel poisoning attack against GraphRAG that corrupts logical/topological structure, expanding the adversarial corruption taxonomy beyond text injection.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused specifically on GraphRAG variant; no defense proposed.

title: KEPo: Knowledge Evolution Poison on Graph-based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Qizhi Chen; Chao Qi; Yihong Huang; Muquan Li; Rongzheng Wang; Dongyang Zhang; Ke Qin; Shuang Liang
why_relevant: Proposes a novel poisoning attack tailored to GraphRAG, exposing vulnerabilities specific to graph-based retrieval-augmented generation.
why_not_or_caveat: Attack-only; no defense or calibration contribution.

title: INTRYGUE: Induction-Aware Entropy Gating for Reliable RAG Uncertainty Estimation
authors: Alexandra Bazarova; Andrei Volodichev; Daria Kotova; Alexey Zaytsev
why_relevant: Proposes a mechanistically grounded uncertainty quantification method for RAG to detect hallucinations, directly addressing calibration and confidence estimation under retrieval grounding.

title: How Large Language Models Balance Internal Knowledge with User and Document Assertions
authors: Shuowei Li; Haoxin Li; Wenda Chu; Yi Fang
why_relevant: Proposes a three-source (parametric, user, document) interaction framework to study knowledge conflict and models' ability to discriminate helpful vs misleading external information, directly relevant to conflict and context compliance.

title: Hidden-in-Plain-Text: A Benchmark for Social-Web Indirect Prompt Injection in RAG
authors: Haoze Guo; Ziqi Wei
why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark and harness for evaluating indirect prompt injection and retrieval poisoning in web-facing RAG, with defenses (sanitization, normalization, attribution-gating) and metrics (ASR, ΔMRR, ΔnDCG).

title: Hidden in the Metadata: Stealth Poisoning Attacks on Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Kennedy Edemacu; Mohammad Mahdi Shokri
why_relevant: Presents a stealth metadata-only poisoning attack against multimodal RAG, evaluates defenses, and exposes retrieval vulnerabilities—directly relevant to the adversarial corruption section.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal RAG; narrower scope than general text RAG poisoning.

title: Grounded Decoding: Retrieval-Anchored Probability Fusion for Faithful RAG
authors: Ibne Farabi Shihab; Fariya Afrin; Sanjeda Akter; Anuj Sharma
why_relevant: Proposes a decoding-time method to enforce grounding in retrieved evidence over parametric knowledge, with adaptive weighting based on distributional conflict and retriever confidence—directly relevant to knowledge conflict and control.

title: Generating Leakage-Free Benchmarks for Robust RAG Evaluation
authors: Jiayi Liu; Jiaxing Zhang; Bowen Jin; Jennifer Neville
why_relevant: Proposes a leakage-free benchmark generation pipeline to isolate retrieval quality from parametric memory, directly addressing evaluation reliability and parametric-vs-retrieved knowledge issues in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on benchmark construction rather than robustness mechanisms per se.

title: Faithfulness-QA: A Counterfactual Entity Substitution Dataset for Training Context-Faithful RAG Models
authors: Li Ju; Junzhe Wang; Qi Zhang
why_relevant: Introduces a large counterfactual entity substitution dataset to train and evaluate RAG models for context-faithfulness under context-vs-parametric knowledge conflicts.
why_not_or_caveat: Primarily a dataset construction paper without new modeling or extensive empirical analysis.

title: Decide Then Retrieve: A Training-Free Framework with Uncertainty-Guided Triggering and Dual-Path Retrieval
authors: Wang Chen; Guanqiang Qi; Weikang Li; Yang Li; Deguo Xia; Jizhou Huang
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: Proposes uncertainty-guided adaptive retrieval triggering and dual-path evidence selection to mitigate retrieval noise, directly addressing when-to-retrieve calibration and noisy retrieval issues.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on open-domain QA performance; does not address adversarial or conflict settings.

title: Can Small Language Models Use What They Retrieve? An Empirical Study of Retrieval Utilization Across Model Scale
authors: Sanchit Pandey
why_relevant: Empirically isolates context utilization failures and distraction effects in small LLMs under oracle and noisy retrieval, directly relevant to distraction and noisy-retrieval robustness analysis.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on small models; diagnostic study rather than proposing defenses.

title: CODE: A Contradiction-Based Deliberation Extension Framework for Overthinking Attacks on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Xiaolei Zhang; Xiaojun Jia; Liquan Chen; Songze Li
why_relevant: Proposes a novel corpus-poisoning attack on RAG that injects contradictory documents to induce overthinking in reasoning models, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and knowledge conflict subtopics.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on inference-cost amplification rather than answer correctness, a narrower attack vector.

title: Bypassing Prompt Injection Detectors through Evasive Injections
authors: Md Jahedur Rahman; Ihsen Alouani

why_relevant: Proposes an adaptive evasion attack against activation-based prompt injection detectors in RAG settings, and a defense via suffix augmentation. Directly relevant to adversarial corruption and defenses for RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on detector evasion rather than retrieval pipeline per se, but framed in RAG threat model.

title: Benchmarking Knowledge-Extraction Attack and Defense on Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zhisheng Qi; Utkarsh Sahu; Li Ma; Haoyu Han; Ryan Rossi; Franck Dernoncourt; Mahantesh Halappanavar; Nesreen Ahmed; Yushun Dong; Yue Zhao; Yu Zhang; Yu Wang
why_relevant: Provides a unified benchmark of knowledge-extraction attacks and defenses on RAG systems, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption and evaluation aspects of the survey.

title: Adversarial Hubness Detector: Detecting Hubness Poisoning in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
authors: Idan Habler; Vineeth Sai Narajala; Stav Koren; Amy Chang; Tiffany Saade
why_relevant: Proposes a detection framework for adversarial hubness poisoning attacks in RAG vector indices, directly addressing retrieval-level adversarial corruption defenses.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses narrowly on embedding-space hub detection rather than broader RAG robustness.

title: Adaptive Stopping for Multi-Turn LLM Reasoning
authors: Xiaofan Zhou; Huy Nguyen; Bo Yu; Chenxi Liu; Lu Cheng
suggested_section: Calibration and control: when to retrieve and abstain
why_relevant: Proposes a conformal prediction framework for adaptive RAG and ReAct that decides when to stop retrieving/reasoning with formal coverage guarantees, including an abstention option. Directly relevant to calibration, control of retrieval, and uncertainty quantification in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on stopping/coverage rather than noisy or adversarial evidence per se.

title: ALDEN: Boosting Private Data Extraction from Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems via Active Learning and Distribution Estimation
authors: Xingyu Lyu; Jianfeng He; Ning Wang; Yidan Hu; Tao Li; Danjue Chen; Shixiong Li; Yimin Chen
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption and Attacks on RAG
why_relevant: Proposes a novel data extraction attack against RAG knowledge bases via prompt injection, active learning, and distribution estimation, directly relevant to adversarial corruption/privacy threats in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy extraction rather than retrieval-integrity attacks; no defense contribution.

title: A Sentence Relation-Based Approach to Sanitizing Malicious Instructions
authors: Soumil Datta; Melissa Umble; Daniel S. Brown; Guanhong Tao
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Defenses against Prompt Injection
why_relevant: SONAR is a sentence-level NLI-based sanitization defense against indirect prompt injection in RAG pipelines, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption section.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on prompt injection defense rather than broader RAG robustness.

title: [] Your RAG is Unfair: Exposing Fairness Vulnerabilities in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Backdoor Attacks
why_relevant: Introduces BiasRAG, a backdoor attack on RAG via compromised query encoders and poisoned documents targeting fairness, expanding the threat landscape of adversarial corruption in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on fairness-specific backdoors rather than general robustness or defenses.

title: TruthfulRAG: Resolving Factual-level Conflicts in Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Knowledge Graphs
authors: Shuyi Liu; Yuming Shang; Xi Zhang
why_relevant: Proposes a KG-based method to resolve factual conflicts between parametric and retrieved knowledge in RAG, directly addressing the knowledge conflict axis of the survey.

title: The Semantic Illusion: Certified Limits of Embedding-Based Hallucination Detection in RAG Systems
authors: Debu Sinha
why_relevant: Applies conformal prediction to RAG hallucination detection, providing finite-sample coverage guarantees and revealing limits of embedding/NLI-based detectors on real hallucinations—directly relevant to calibration, abstention, and evaluation in robust RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is narrow on detector calibration; does not address retrieval noise or attacks.

title: The Hidden Threat in Plain Text: Attacking RAG Data Loaders
authors: Alberto Castagnaro; Umberto Salviati; Mauro Conti; Luca Pajola; Simeone Pizzi
why_relevant: Introduces novel poisoning attacks targeting RAG data loaders via content obfuscation/injection in DOCX/HTML/PDF, with taxonomy and evaluation across loaders and end-to-end RAG systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on ingestion-stage attacks rather than defenses or calibration.

title: Separate the Wheat from the Chaff: Winnowing Down Divergent Views in Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Song Wang; Zihan Chen; Peng Wang; Zhepei Wei; Zhen Tan; Yu Meng; Cong Shen; Jundong Li
why_relevant: WinnowRAG addresses noisy retrieval by clustering and iteratively filtering irrelevant/misleading documents via a multi-agent critic framework, directly targeting robustness to retrieval noise.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on noise filtering only; does not address adversarial attacks, conflicts, or calibration.

title: Search Wisely: Mitigating Sub-optimal Agentic Searches By Reducing Uncertainty
authors: Peilin Wu; Mian Zhang; Xinlu Zhang; Xinya Du; Zhiyu Zoey Chen
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: Studies when an agentic RAG system should retrieve vs. rely on parametric knowledge, linking sub-optimal search to uncertainty about knowledge boundaries, and proposes an RL method (β-GRPO) using confidence thresholds to control retrieval decisions.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on agentic search efficiency rather than handling noisy/adversarial evidence directly.

title: SciRerankBench: Benchmarking Rerankers Towards Scientific Retrieval-Augmented Generated LLMs
authors: Haotian Chen; Qingqing Long; Meng Xiao; Xiao Luo; Wei Ju; Chengrui Wang; Xuezhi Wang; Yuanchun Zhou; Hengshu Zhu
why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark evaluating rerankers in RAG with noisy contexts, semantically similar but logically irrelevant contexts, and counterfactual contexts—directly relevant to noise, distraction, and conflict robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to scientific QA and focused on reranker evaluation rather than end-to-end RAG robustness methods.

title: SUGAR: Leveraging Contextual Confidence for Smarter Retrieval
authors: Hanna Zubkova; Ji-Hoon Park; Seong-Whan Lee
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: SUGAR uses semantic entropy to decide when to retrieve and whether to do single- vs multi-step retrieval, directly addressing the 'when to retrieve' calibration/control question and avoiding distraction by noisy retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on adaptive retrieval triggering rather than handling noise/conflict/adversaries within retrieved evidence.

title: RoseRAG: Robust Retrieval-augmented Generation with Small-scale LLMs via Margin-aware Preference Optimization
authors: Tianci Liu; Haoxiang Jiang; Tianze Wang; Ran Xu; Yue Yu; Linjun Zhang; Tuo Zhao; Haoyu Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a preference optimization method to make small LLMs robust to noisy retrieved documents in RAG, directly addressing noisy retrieval robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on SLMs and training strategy; limited scope beyond noise robustness.

title: Robustness via Referencing: Defending against Prompt Injection Attacks by Referencing the Executed Instruction
authors: Yulin Chen; Haoran Li; Yuan Sui; Yue Liu; Yufei He; Xiaoling Bai; Chi Fei; Yabo Li; Haozhe Ma; Yangqiu Song; Bryan Hooi

why_relevant: Proposes a defense against indirect prompt injection attacks where malicious instructions are embedded in retrieved content, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on prompt injection broadly rather than RAG-specific poisoning pipelines.

authors: Jiawei Liu; Zhuo Chen; Rui Zhu; Miaokun Chen; Yuyang Gong; Wei Lu; Xiaofeng Wang

why_relevant: Proposes a certified defense (RobustMask) against adversarial ranking attacks on neural retrievers used in RAG pipelines, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.

authors: Shi-Qi Yan; Quan Liu; Zhen-Hua Ling

authors: Austin Jia; Avaneesh Ramesh; Zain Shamsi; Daniel Zhang; Alex Liu

authors: Shiping Yang; Jie Wu; Wenbiao Ding; Ning Wu; Shining Liang; Ming Gong; Hongzhi Li; Hengyuan Zhang; Angel X. Chang; Dongmei Zhang

authors: Debashish Chakraborty; Eugene Yang; Daniel Khashabi; Dawn Lawrie; Kevin Duh
why_relevant: Applies split conformal prediction to filter retrieved snippets with finite-sample coverage guarantees, directly addressing noisy retrieval and calibrated control over context.

authors: Philhoon Oh; Jinwoo Shin; James Thorne
why_relevant: Proposes KV-Fusion to make RAG position-invariant, addressing lost-in-the-middle distraction and improving robustness to irrelevant passages.

authors: Hanyu Zhu; Lance Fiondella; Jiawei Yuan; Kai Zeng; Long Jiao

authors: Kaiwen Zuo; Zelin Liu; Raman Dutt; Ziyang Wang; Zhongtian Sun; Fan Mo; Pietro Liò
