why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific to code generation rather than general QA RAG.

title: Energy Landscapes Enable Reliable Abstention in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Healthcare
authors: Ravi Shankar; Sheng Wong; Lin Li; Magdalena Bachmann; Alex Silverthorne; Beth Albert; Gabriel Davis Jones
why_relevant: Proposes an energy-based abstention mechanism for RAG that detects OOD/near-distribution queries and triggers abstention, directly addressing calibration, uncertainty, and when-not-to-answer control in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (women's health) and focuses on query-level OOD rather than retrieved-evidence robustness.

title: EmoRAG: Evaluating RAG Robustness to Symbolic Perturbations
authors: Xinyun Zhou; Xinfeng Li; Yinan Peng; Ming Xu; Xuanwang Zhang; Miao Yu; Yidong Wang; Xiaojun Jia; Kun Wang; Qingsong Wen; XiaoFeng Wang; Wei Dong
why_relevant: Reveals a symbolic-perturbation attack vector against RAG retrievers via emoticon injection, evaluates defenses, and proposes detection — directly relevant to adversarial robustness of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Narrowly focused on emoticon-based perturbations rather than broader poisoning/injection literature.

title: END: Early Noise Dropping for Efficient and Effective Context Denoising
authors: Hongye Jin; Pei Chen; Jingfeng Yang; Zhengyang Wang; Fangran Mo; Jinghan Zhang; Meng Jiang; Yifan Gao; Binxuan Huang; Xinyang Zhang; Zheng Li; Tianyi Liu; Huasheng Li; Bing Yin
why_relevant: Proposes a method to detect and drop noisy/distracting chunks in RAG and long-context inputs using early-layer probers, directly addressing distraction and noisy retrieval robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on efficiency-aware denoising rather than adversarial or conflict settings.

title: Dynamic Context Selection for Retrieval-Augmented Generation: Mitigating Distractors and Positional Bias
authors: Malika Iratni; Mohand Boughanem; Taoufiq Dkaki
why_relevant: Analyzes distractor impact and positional bias in RAG, and proposes a classifier to dynamically select retrieval size, directly addressing distraction and adaptive retrieval control.
why_not_or_caveat: Limited to MuSiQue and a simple classifier; not a foundational work.

title: Do Retrieval-Augmented Language Models Adapt to Varying User Needs?
authors: Peilin Wu; Xinlu Zhang; Wenhao Yu; Xingyu Liu; Xinya Du; Zhiyu Zoey Chen
why_relevant: Introduces an evaluation framework assessing RALMs across user-instruction modes (Context-Exclusive/First, Memory-First) under context matching, knowledge conflict, and irrelevant retrieval, directly addressing conflict resolution, instruction compliance, and robustness to noisy context.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on user-need adaptation rather than novel defenses; adversarial coverage is limited to counterfactual context.

title: Defending Against Knowledge Poisoning Attacks During Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Kennedy Edemacu; Vinay M. Shashidhar; Micheal Tuape; Dan Abudu; Beakcheol Jang; Jong Wook Kim
why_relevant: Proposes filtration-based defenses (FilterRAG, ML-FilterRAG) against PoisonedRAG knowledge poisoning attacks, directly addressing adversarial corruption of RAG knowledge bases.
why_not_or_caveat: Narrowly targets PoisonedRAG-style attacks; relies on a specific statistical property.

title: Copy-Paste to Mitigate Large Language Model Hallucinations
authors: Yongchao Long; Xian Wu; Yingying Zhang; Xianbin Wen; Yuxi Zhou; Shenda Hong
why_relevant: Proposes a training method (CopyPasteLLM) to improve contextual faithfulness under knowledge conflict, addressing the parametric-vs-contextual conflict problem central to robust RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on faithfulness/hallucination mitigation rather than broader robustness like noise or adversarial attacks.

title: Confidence-Based Response Abstinence: Improving LLM Trustworthiness via Activation-Based Uncertainty Estimation
authors: Zhiqi Huang; Vivek Datla; Chenyang Zhu; Alfy Samuel; Daben Liu; Anoop Kumar; Ritesh Soni
why_relevant: Proposes activation-based confidence estimation for RAG to enable response abstention, directly addressing calibration and abstain-control under uncertain/ambiguous evidence in production RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (financial customer support) and limited public benchmarking.

title: Bridging External and Parametric Knowledge: Mitigating Hallucination of LLMs with Shared-Private Semantic Synergy in Dual-Stream Knowledge
authors: Yi Sui; Chaozhuo Li; Chen Zhang; Dawei song; Qiuchi Li
suggested_section: Knowledge Conflict and Adaptive Retrieval Control
why_relevant: Proposes a RAG framework explicitly addressing context-memory and inter-context conflicts, noise filtering of retrieved evidence, and unsupervised hallucination detection to decide when to retrieve.

title: Benchmarking Multimodal Knowledge Conflict for Large Multimodal Models
authors: Yifan Jia; Kailin Jiang; Yuyang Liang; Qihan Ren; Yi Xin; Rui Yang; Fenze Feng; Mingcai Chen; Hengyang Lu; Haozhe Wang; Xiaoye Qu; Dongrui Liu; Lizhen Cui; Yuntao Du
why_relevant: Introduces MMKC-Bench for evaluating context-memory and inter-context knowledge conflicts in multimodal RAG, finding LMMs over-rely on parametric knowledge.
why_not_or_caveat: Multimodal focus; may be tangential to text-centric RAG sections.

title: AttnTrace: Contextual Attribution of Prompt Injection and Knowledge Corruption
authors: Yanting Wang; Runpeng Geng; Ying Chen; Jinyuan Jia
why_relevant: Proposes an attention-based context traceback method to localize injected/malicious texts in RAG and long-context inputs, supporting post-attack forensics and improving prompt injection detection.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on attribution/traceback rather than preventing the attack itself.

title: Accommodate Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval-augmented LLMs: Towards Robust Response Generation in the Wild
authors: Jiatai Wang; Zhiwei Xu; Di Jin; Xuewen Yang; Tao Li
why_relevant: Proposes a theoretical and methodological framework (Swin-VIB) to handle knowledge conflicts between parametric memory and retrieved context in RAG, with uncertainty analysis.

title: Supportiveness-based Knowledge Rewriting for Retrieval-augmented Language Modeling
authors: Zile Qiao; Wei Ye; Yong Jiang; Tong Mo; Pengjun Xie; Weiping Li; Fei Huang; Shikun Zhang
why_relevant: Proposes a knowledge rewriter that filters noisy/misleading retrieved content using a supportiveness score, directly addressing robustness of RAG to unreliable retrieved evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on rewriting/compression rather than conflict, attacks, or calibration explicitly.

title: SecAlign: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Preference Optimization
authors: Sizhe Chen; Arman Zharmagambetov; Saeed Mahloujifar; Kamalika Chaudhuri; David Wagner; Chuan Guo
why_relevant: SecAlign defends LLMs against prompt injection from external data sources (including retrieved content) via preference optimization, directly relevant to adversarial corruption defenses in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on general LLM-integrated applications rather than RAG specifically, but threat model includes web retrieval.

title: REAR: A Relevance-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Framework for Open-Domain Question Answering
authors: Yuhao Wang; Ruiyang Ren; Junyi Li; Wayne Xin Zhao; Jing Liu; Ji-Rong Wen
why_relevant: REAR addresses noisy/irrelevant retrieval by adding a relevance assessment module and noise-resistant training, enabling the LLM to adaptively weigh external vs parametric knowledge.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on open-domain QA; does not address adversarial or OOD settings.

title: Prompt Perturbation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation based Large Language Models
authors: Zhibo Hu; Chen Wang; Yanfeng Shu; Helen; Paik; Liming Zhu
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption and attacks on RAG
why_relevant: Proposes Gradient Guided Prompt Perturbation, an adversarial prefix attack targeting RAG retrieval to induce factually incorrect outputs, plus a neuron-activation-based detection defense. Directly addresses adversarial robustness of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on prompt-side perturbations rather than corpus poisoning; defense is detection-based.

title: Parenting: Optimizing Knowledge Selection of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with Parameter Decoupling and Tailored Tuning
authors: Yongxin Xu; Ruizhe Zhang; Xinke Jiang; Yujie Feng; Yuzhen Xiao; Xinyu Ma; Runchuan Zhu; Xu Chu; Junfeng Zhao; Yasha Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a parameter-decoupling fine-tuning method to balance adherence to retrieved context vs robustness to noisy contexts, directly tackling knowledge conflict and noisy retrieval in RAG.

title: KnowPO: Knowledge-aware Preference Optimization for Controllable Knowledge Selection in Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Ruizhe Zhang; Yongxin Xu; Yuzhen Xiao; Runchuan Zhu; Xinke Jiang; Xu Chu; Junfeng Zhao; Yasha Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a preference optimization approach for balancing adherence to retrieved context and robustness to noise under knowledge conflicts, directly addressing context vs parametric conflicts and noisy retrieval.

title: Investigating Context-Faithfulness in Large Language Models: The Roles of Memory Strength and Evidence Style
authors: Yuepei Li; Kang Zhou; Qiao Qiao; Bach Nguyen; Qing Wang; Qi Li
why_relevant: Analyzes context faithfulness of LLMs under knowledge conflicts, quantifying memory strength and the effect of evidence style on receptiveness to retrieved evidence.

title: Get my drift? Catching LLM Task Drift with Activation Deltas
authors: Sahar Abdelnabi; Aideen Fay; Giovanni Cherubin; Ahmed Salem; Mario Fritz; Andrew Paverd
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption: defenses against indirect prompt injection
why_relevant: Proposes activation-delta probing to detect indirect prompt injection (task drift) in retrieval-augmented LLMs, directly addressing adversarial corruption of retrieved evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on prompt injection detection generally rather than RAG-specific retrieval pipeline robustness.

title: Entropy-Based Decoding for Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models
authors: Zexuan Qiu; Zijing Ou; Bin Wu; Jingjing Li; Aiwei Liu; Irwin King
why_relevant: Proposes an entropy-based decoding method to mitigate distraction from noisy retrieved documents and conflicts with parametric knowledge in RAG, directly addressing robustness under unreliable evidence.

title: Enhancing Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Language Models with In-Context Learning
authors: Seong-Il Park; Seung-Woo Choi; Na-Hyun Kim; Jay-Yoon Lee
why_relevant: Proposes in-context learning with MRC and conflict demonstrations to make RALMs more robust to unanswerable queries and conflicting retrieved contexts, directly addressing noisy retrieval and knowledge conflict.
why_not_or_caveat: Method is relatively lightweight; experiments limited to NQ and WebQ.

title: Dialectical Alignment: Resolving the Tension of 3H and Security Threats of LLMs
authors: Shu Yang; Jiayuan Su; Han Jiang; Mengdi Li; Keyuan Cheng; Muhammad Asif Ali; Lijie Hu; Di Wang
why_relevant: Proposes alignment-based defense against poisoned context attacks in RAG while balancing context-memory and inter-context conflicts, directly addressing knowledge conflict and adversarial corruption.

title: Defense Against Prompt Injection Attack by Leveraging Attack Techniques
authors: Yulin Chen; Haoran Li; Zihao Zheng; Yangqiu Song; Dekai Wu; Bryan Hooi
suggested_section: Adversarial corruption: defenses against prompt injection
why_relevant: Proposes training-free defenses against indirect prompt injection attacks, including those embedded in retrieved content, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG inputs.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is general prompt injection rather than RAG-specific poisoning, but indirect injection via retrieved data is a key threat model.

title: DYNAMICQA: Tracing Internal Knowledge Conflicts in Language Models
authors: Sara Vera Marjanović; Haeun Yu; Pepa Atanasova; Maria Maistro; Christina Lioma; Isabelle Augenstein
why_relevant: Introduces DynamicQA, a benchmark for studying intra-memory and context-memory knowledge conflicts with realistic temporal/disputable facts, directly relevant to RAG's struggle with conflicting evidence and parametric vs. contextual knowledge.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is more on intra-memory conflict and semantic entropy than on retrieval pipeline robustness per se.

title: Blinded by Generated Contexts: How Language Models Merge Generated and Retrieved Contexts When Knowledge Conflicts?
authors: Hexiang Tan; Fei Sun; Wanli Yang; Yuanzhuo Wang; Qi Cao; Xueqi Cheng
why_relevant: Studies how LLMs resolve conflicts between generated and retrieved contexts, revealing bias toward generated contexts even when incorrect. Directly relevant to retrieved-vs-retrieved/source conflict and context compliance issues in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on generated vs retrieved context conflict rather than classical parametric-vs-retrieved conflict.

title: Answerability in Retrieval-Augmented Open-Domain Question Answering
authors: Rustam Abdumalikov; Pasquale Minervini; Yova Kementchedjhieva
suggested_section: Calibration and Abstention under Noisy Retrieval
why_relevant: Studies answerability/abstention in RAG-based ODQA, showing that models trained with random negatives fail on semantically related but irrelevant excerpts, and proposes training with SQuAD 2.0 unanswerable pairs to improve abstention.
why_not_or_caveat: Narrow extractive QA focus with T5 models; limited scope.

title: Adaptive Contrastive Decoding in Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Handling Noisy Contexts
authors: Youna Kim; Hyuhng Joon Kim; Cheonbok Park; Choonghyun Park; Hyunsoo Cho; Junyeob Kim; Kang Min Yoo; Sang-goo Lee; Taeuk Kim
why_relevant: Proposes an entropy-based adaptive contrastive decoding method to control reliance on retrieved context vs parametric knowledge, specifically targeting robustness to noisy retrieved contexts in RAG.

title: RECOMP: Improving Retrieval-Augmented LMs with Compression and Selective Augmentation
authors: Fangyuan Xu; Weijia Shi; Eunsol Choi
why_relevant: RECOMP compresses retrieved documents and supports selective augmentation (returning empty when retrieval is irrelevant), directly addressing noisy/distracting retrieval and when-to-trust-retrieval control in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Primary motivation is efficiency; robustness is a secondary benefit.

title: Merging Generated and Retrieved Knowledge for Open-Domain QA
authors: Yunxiang Zhang; Muhammad Khalifa; Lajanugen Logeswaran; Moontae Lee; Honglak Lee; Lu Wang
why_relevant: Proposes COMBO to resolve conflicts between LLM-generated and retrieved passages, directly addressing knowledge conflict in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on parametric-vs-retrieved conflict in ODQA; not on adversarial or noisy retrieval per se.

title: QuCo-RAG: Quantifying Uncertainty from the Pre-training Corpus for Dynamic Retrieval-Augmented Generation
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: Proposes a dynamic RAG triggering mechanism based on pre-training corpus statistics to decide when to retrieve, addressing miscalibration of internal confidence signals and long-tail knowledge gaps.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on retrieval triggering rather than handling noisy/adversarial evidence directly.

title: [] Spa-VLM: Stealthy Poisoning Attacks on RAG-based VLM
why_relevant: Proposes a stealthy poisoning attack on multi-modal RAG-based VLMs, injecting adversarial image-text pairs into the knowledge base to mislead generation, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on VLM/multimodal setting rather than text-only RAG.

title: [] HV-Attack: Hierarchical Visual Attack for Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation
why_relevant: Proposes a visual adversarial attack on multimodal RAG that disrupts both retriever and generator via imperceptible image perturbations, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of RAG systems.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal RAG attacks; no defense or calibration aspect.

title: [] Does Vec2Text Pose a New Corpus Poisoning Threat?
why_relevant: Proposes a novel corpus poisoning attack against dense retrievers using Vec2Text embedding inversion, which doesn't require model weights and can scale, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on dense retriever poisoning rather than end-to-end RAG generation, but retrieval poisoning is a key threat vector.

title: [] Data Extraction Attacks in Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Backdoors
why_relevant: Proposes a backdoor-based data extraction attack on RAG systems, exposing privacy vulnerabilities in retrieval databases through poisoned fine-tuning.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on privacy extraction rather than answer-correctness robustness, but fits adversarial corruption scope.

title: [] Black-Box Opinion Manipulation Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box adversarial ranking poisoning attack on RAG targeting opinion manipulation in open-ended controversial topics, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused narrowly on opinion-polarity manipulation rather than factual QA poisoning.

title: [] Bias Amplification in RAG: Poisoning Knowledge Retrieval to Steer LLMs
why_relevant: Proposes a poisoning attack on RAG that manipulates retrieval to amplify model biases, plus a dual-stage defense, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus on fairness/bias amplification rather than factual correctness, a narrower angle than typical RAG poisoning.

title: TRAQ: Trustworthy Retrieval Augmented Question Answering via Conformal Prediction
why_relevant: TRAQ applies conformal prediction to RAG to provide statistical coverage guarantees on answer correctness, addressing uncertainty in both retrieval and generation stages.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on coverage guarantees rather than robustness to noise/attacks directly.

title: RE-RAG: Improving Open-Domain QA Performance and Interpretability with Relevance Estimator in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
suggested_section: Calibration and control / filtering noisy retrieval
why_relevant: Proposes a relevance estimator that filters irrelevant retrieved contexts, provides confidence-based decoding strategies including abstention ('unanswerable') and falling back to parametric knowledge, directly addressing distraction by noisy retrieval and calibration/control.

title: Pandora: Jailbreak GPTs by Retrieval Augmented Generation Poisoning
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Indirect Prompt Injection
why_relevant: PANDORA introduces a RAG poisoning attack vector that uses maliciously crafted documents to indirectly jailbreak GPTs, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval sources.
why_not_or_caveat: Preliminary evaluation only; focused on jailbreak rather than general RAG robustness.

title: FlipedRAG: Black-Box Opinion Manipulation Attacks to Retrieval-Augmented Generation of Large Language Models
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Retrieval Attacks
why_relevant: Proposes a black-box poisoning/opinion-manipulation attack against RAG retrievers, demonstrating corpus poisoning vulnerabilities and evaluating defenses.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on opinion manipulation rather than general factual robustness; defenses analysis is limited.

title: CONFLARE: CONFormal LArge language model REtrieval
why_relevant: Applies conformal prediction to RAG retrieval to quantify uncertainty and set similarity thresholds with statistical coverage guarantees, directly relevant to calibration/control and uncertainty quantification in retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on retrieval-side calibration only, with a small medical QA demonstration.

title: C-RAG: Certified Generation Risks for Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
why_relevant: C-RAG provides conformal risk control for RAG generation, certifying upper bounds on generation risks including under test-time distribution shifts, directly relevant to calibration and uncertainty in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on certified risk guarantees rather than specific noise/conflict/adversarial scenarios.

title: When to Trust: A Causality-Aware Calibration Framework for Accurate Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jing Ren; Bowen Li; Ziqi Xu; Xikun Zhang; Haytham Fayek; Xiaodong Li
why_relevant: Proposes a calibration framework for KG-RAG addressing overconfidence under unreliable/incomplete retrieved subgraphs, using counterfactual prompting and re-scoring to better align confidence with correctness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on KG-RAG specifically rather than general text RAG.

title: Can LLMs Take Retrieved Information with a Grain of Salt?
authors: Behzad Shayegh; Mohamed Osama Ahmed; Fred Tung; Leo Feng
why_relevant: Proposes a formal metric and interaction strategy for LLMs to adapt RAG outputs to retrieved-context certainty, addressing calibration, uncertainty handling, and prior-vs-context conflict—core themes of the survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Assumes externally provided certainty scores rather than estimating them; focused on obedience to scores rather than retrieval robustness per se.

title: Semantic Grounding Index: Geometric Bounds on Context Engagement in RAG Systems
authors: Javier Marín
why_relevant: Proposes a geometric, calibration-friendly signal (SGI) for detecting ungrounded/hallucinated RAG responses, directly relevant to detection, abstention, and calibration under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Measures topical engagement rather than factual accuracy (negative result on TruthfulQA); limited to single-signal detection.

title: RAG Security and Privacy: Formalizing the Threat Model and Attack Surface
why_relevant: Proposes a formal threat model and taxonomy for RAG attacks including poisoning and membership inference, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption section.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on security/privacy formalization rather than defenses or robustness mechanisms; limited coverage of other survey dimensions.

title: With Argus Eyes: Assessing Retrieval Gaps via Uncertainty Scoring to Detect and Remedy Retrieval Blind Spots
authors: Zeinab Sadat Taghavi; Ali Modarressi; Hinrich Schutze; Andreas Marfurt
why_relevant: Identifies systematic retriever blind spots—missing relevant evidence due to embedding geometry—and proposes an uncertainty score (RPS) plus augmentation remedy, directly addressing retrieval failures that undermine RAG robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on the retriever side rather than generator-side robustness; touches calibration only indirectly.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Multimodal Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Simon Binz; Heydar Soudani; Faegheh Hasibi
why_relevant: Proposes a learnable uncertainty quantification method for multimodal RAG that captures uncertainty from retrieval and modality inputs, directly relevant to calibration and reliability under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal VQA setting; not addressing adversarial or conflict aspects.

title: Toward Robust GraphRAG: Mitigating Retrieval Drift and Hallucination from Imperfect Knowledge Graphs
authors: Yizhuo Ma; Jinchuan Xu; Tao Wen; Qizhi Chen; Jiakai Li; Rongzheng Wang; Muquan Li; Shuang Liang; Ke Qin
why_relevant: Addresses robustness of GraphRAG under imperfect/noisy KGs with spurious noise and incomplete information, using sufficiency checks to decide when to fall back to textual recovery—relevant to noisy retrieval and control mechanisms.
why_not_or_caveat: Specific to GraphRAG/KG construction errors rather than general RAG noise.

title: To Copy or Not to Copy: Copying Is Easier to Induce Than Recall
authors: Mehrdad Farahani; Franziska Penzkofer; Richard Johansson
why_relevant: Mechanistic study of how LLMs arbitrate between parametric knowledge and (false) retrieved context, with a steering intervention to shift copy-vs-recall behavior. Directly addresses knowledge conflict and context compliance in RAG settings.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is mechanistic/interventional rather than proposing a deployable RAG robustness method.

title: The Cost of Context: Mitigating Textual Bias in Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Hoin Jung; Xiaoqian Wang
why_relevant: Identifies 'recorruption' in multimodal RAG where even oracle context degrades correct predictions due to attention collapse and positional bias, and proposes an inference-time mitigation (BAIR). Directly relevant to distraction and context-vs-internal-knowledge conflict in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal (MLLM) setting rather than pure text RAG.

title: The Confidence Dichotomy: Analyzing and Mitigating Miscalibration in Tool-Use Agents
authors: Weihao Xuan; Qingcheng Zeng; Heli Qi; Yunze Xiao; Junjue Wang; Naoto Yokoya
why_relevant: Studies how noisy evidence retrieval (web search) induces overconfidence in tool-use agents and proposes an RL framework to jointly optimize accuracy and calibration, directly relevant to calibration under unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Framed as tool-use agents rather than RAG specifically, but evidence-tool analysis maps directly to retrieval noise.

title: Tackling the Inherent Difficulty of Noise Filtering in RAG
authors: Jingyu Liu; Jiaen Lin; Yong Liu
why_relevant: Proposes a fine-tuning method to make LLMs robust to noisy/irrelevant retrieved documents, with theoretical analysis of why noise filtering is hard. Directly addresses noisy retrieval robustness.

title: Skill-RAG: Failure-State-Aware Retrieval Augmentation via Hidden-State Probing and Skill Routing
authors: Kai Wei; Raymond Li; Xi Zhu; Zhaoqian Xue; Jiaojiao Han; Jingcheng Niu; Fan Yang
why_relevant: Skill-RAG uses hidden-state probing to detect retrieval failure states and routes among corrective skills (rewrite, decompose, focus, exit), directly addressing adaptive retrieval control, abstention, and query-evidence misalignment under OOD conditions.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on failure-recovery routing rather than adversarial or conflict settings; does not address poisoning or knowledge conflict.

title: Retromorphic Testing with Hierarchical Verification for Hallucination Detection in RAG
authors: Boxi Yu; Yuzhong Zhang; Liting Lin; Lionel Briand; Emir Muñoz
why_relevant: Proposes a hallucination/faithfulness detector for RAG that flags unsupported or contradicted claims against retrieved context, and introduces an enhanced RAGTruth benchmark. Relevant to evaluation of context-faithfulness and detection of conflicts between generation and retrieved evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on post-hoc detection rather than mitigating noisy/adversarial retrieval directly.

title: Rethinking the Reranker: Boundary-Aware Evidence Selection for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Jiashuo Sun; Pengcheng Jiang; Saizhuo Wang; Jiajun Fan; Heng Wang; Siru Ouyang; Ming Zhong; Yizhu Jiao; Chengsong Huang; Xueqiang Xu; Pengrui Han; Peiran Li; Jiaxin Huang; Ge Liu; Heng Ji; Jiawei Han
why_relevant: BAR-RAG addresses RAG brittleness under noisy retrieval by training a boundary-aware reranker/selector using generator uncertainty, directly targeting robustness and evidence filtering.

title: Rethinking the Necessity of Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented Generation through the Lens of Adaptive Listwise Ranking
authors: Jun Feng; Jiahui Tang; Zhicheng He; Hang Lv; Hongchao Gu; Hao Wang; Xuezhi Yang; Shuai Fang
why_relevant: Proposes an adaptive listwise reranker with passage dropout that filters noisy retrieved passages and decides when retrieval is unnecessary, directly addressing noise filtering and adaptive retrieval control in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on efficiency/adaptive ranking rather than adversarial or conflict robustness.

title: ReFilter: Improving Robustness of Retrieval-Augmented Generation via Gated Filter
authors: Yixin Chen; Ying Xiong; Shangyu Wu; Xiangrui Ke; Nan Guan; Chun Jason Xue
suggested_section: Noisy Retrieval: Filtering and Fusion Methods
why_relevant: Proposes a token-level gated filter to suppress irrelevant/redundant/conflicting retrieved tokens, directly addressing noisy retrieval and distraction in RAG and analyzing the recall-vs-performance decoupling as k grows.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on latent-fusion architecture; does not address adversarial attacks or calibration.

title: Purifying Multimodal Retrieval: Fragment-Level Evidence Selection for RAG
authors: Xihang Wang; Zihan Wang; Chengkai Huang; Cao Liu; Ke Zeng; Quan Z. Sheng; Lina Yao
why_relevant: Proposes fragment-level evidence selection to purify noisy multimodal retrieval, directly addressing distraction and irrelevant content within retrieved documents in MRAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal setting and selection method rather than broader robustness taxonomy.

title: OpenDecoder: Open Large Language Model Decoding to Incorporate Document Quality in RAG
authors: Fengran Mo; Zhan Su; Yuchen Hui; Jinghan Zhang; Jia Ao Sun; Zheyuan Liu; Chao Zhang; Tetsuya Sakai; Jian-Yun Nie
why_relevant: Proposes a decoding method that integrates explicit document relevance/QPP signals to make RAG robust to noisy retrieved contexts, directly addressing noisy retrieval and control over evidence trust.

title: Multimodal Adaptive Retrieval Augmented Generation through Internal Representation Learning
authors: Ruoshuang Du; Xin Sun; Qiang Liu; Bowen Song; Zhongqi Chen; Weiqiang Wang; Liang Wang
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: Proposes adaptive retrieval for multimodal RAG that uses internal representations to decide when retrieved evidence is harmful vs helpful, directly addressing noisy/misleading retrieval and when-to-retrieve calibration.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on multimodal VQA with reverse image retrieval, narrower than text RAG.

title: MIPIAD: Multilingual Indirect Prompt Injection Attack Defense with Qwen -- TF-IDF Hybrid and Meta-Ensemble Learning
authors: Al Muhit Muhtadi; Mostafa Rifat Tazwar
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Indirect Prompt Injection Defenses
why_relevant: Proposes a multilingual defense against indirect prompt injection in RAG/tool-using LLMs and provides a large benchmark built on BIPIA, directly relevant to the adversarial corruption axis of the survey.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on input classification rather than RAG pipeline integration; empirical scope limited to English and Bangla.

title: LeakDojo: Decoding the Leakage Threats of RAG Systems
authors: Maosen Zhang; Jianshuo Dong; Boting Lu; Wenyue Li; Xiaoping Zhang; Tianwei Zhang; Han Qiu
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption and Attacks on RAG
why_relevant: LeakDojo provides a configurable framework benchmarking RAG leakage attacks and defenses, directly relevant to adversarial corruption and evaluation of RAG robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on data extraction/leakage rather than poisoning or generation correctness, a narrower slice of adversarial RAG threats.

title: LatentAudit: Real-Time White-Box Faithfulness Monitoring for Retrieval-Augmented Generation with Verifiable Deployment
authors: Zhe Yu; Wenpeng Xing; Meng Han
why_relevant: Proposes a real-time faithfulness monitor for RAG that flags unsupported answers under contradictions, retrieval misses, and partial-support noise, directly relevant to calibration/abstention and robustness to unreliable evidence.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus on internal-state monitoring and verifiable deployment; zk-proof aspect is tangential to the survey.

title: Know When You're Wrong: Aligning Confidence with Correctness for LLM Error Detection
authors: Xie Xiaohu; Liu Xiaohu; Yao Benjamin
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: Proposes a normalized confidence score and self-evaluation for LLM error detection, with direct application to adaptive RAG (selective retrieval when uncertain). Also analyzes calibration impacts of SFT/RL/DPO and proposes a fix.
why_not_or_caveat: Adaptive RAG is a demonstration rather than the primary focus; broader scope is general LLM calibration.

title: K-FinHallu: A Hallucination Detection Benchmark for Multi-Turn RAG in Korean Finance
authors: Eunbyeol Cho; Yunseung Lee; Mirae Kim; Jeewon Yang; Youngjun Kwak; Edward Choi
why_relevant: Introduces a multi-turn RAG hallucination detection benchmark with a taxonomy covering contradictions, unverifiable claims, irrelevance, and justified abstention—directly relevant to evaluating RAG robustness, context faithfulness, and refusal calibration.
why_not_or_caveat: Domain-specific (Korean finance), which may limit generality.

title: ICON: Indirect Prompt Injection Defense for Agents based on Inference-Time Correction
authors: Che Wang; Fuyao Zhang; Jiaming Zhang; Ziqi Zhang; Yinghui Wang; Longtao Huang; Jianbo Gao; Zhong Chen; Wei Yang Bryan Lim
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Indirect Prompt Injection Defenses
why_relevant: Proposes an inference-time defense against indirect prompt injection attacks in tool-augmented LLM agents, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieved content in RAG-style settings.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on agent tool-use rather than classical RAG QA; relevance to retrieval robustness is via IPI in retrieved content.

title: How You Ask Matters! Adaptive RAG Robustness to Query Variations
authors: Yunah Jang; Megha Sundriyal; Kyomin Jung; Meeyoung Cha
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: Introduces a benchmark evaluating Adaptive RAG robustness to semantically equivalent query variations, measuring stability of retrieval decisions (when to retrieve) and answer quality—directly relevant to calibration/control and evaluation under unreliable inputs.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on query-side variation rather than evidence-side noise/conflict/attacks.

title: How Retrieved Context Shapes Internal Representations in RAG
authors: Samuel Yeh; Sharon Li
why_relevant: Analyzes how relevant, distracting, and random retrieved documents shape LLM internal representations and downstream behavior in RAG, connecting noise/distraction to abstention and parametric-vs-retrieved interactions.
why_not_or_caveat: Representation-level analysis rather than a new robustness method or benchmark.

title: Hidden in Memory: Sleeper Memory Poisoning in LLM Agents
authors: Sidharth Pulipaka; Stanislau Hlebik; Leonidas Raghav; Sahar Abdelnabi; Vyas Raina; Ivaxi Sheth; Mario Fritz
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Poisoning and Indirect Prompt Injection
why_relevant: Studies indirect prompt injection that poisons persistent memory of LLM agents, causing delayed retrieval-driven malicious behavior. Relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieval/memory stores in RAG-like pipelines.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on agent memory rather than classic RAG corpora; relevance is via analogy to retrieval poisoning and indirect injection.

title: Fact-Checking with Large Language Models via Probabilistic Certainty and Consistency
authors: Haoran Wang; Maryam Khalid; Qiong Wu; Jian Gao; Cheng Cao
suggested_section: Calibration and Control: When to Retrieve
why_relevant: Proposes a confidence-based adaptive routing mechanism deciding when to rely on parametric knowledge vs trigger retrieval/deep search, directly addressing calibration and control of retrieval under uncertainty.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on fact-checking rather than general RAG QA; robustness to noisy/adversarial evidence not the central concern.

title: Facet-Level Tracing of Evidence Uncertainty and Hallucination in RAG
authors: Passant Elchafei; Monorama Swain; Shahed Masoudian; Markus Schedl
suggested_section: Evaluation and Diagnostics of Evidence Usage
why_relevant: Introduces a facet-level diagnostic framework that traces evidence uncertainty and retrieval-generation misalignment in RAG, characterizing failure modes such as evidence absence, misalignment, and parametric-knowledge overrides. Directly relevant to knowledge conflict, uncertainty, and evaluation of RAG faithfulness.
why_not_or_caveat: Diagnostic/analysis rather than a defense or new method; limited datasets.

title: EnterpriseRAG-Bench: A RAG Benchmark for Company Internal Knowledge
authors: Yuhong Sun; Joachim Rahmfeld; Chris Weaver; Weijia Chen; Roshan Desai; Wenxi Huang; Mark H. Butler
why_relevant: Introduces an enterprise RAG benchmark explicitly featuring noisy/misfiled documents, near-duplicates, conflicting information, and 'info not found' questions testing abstention—directly aligned with robustness, conflict resolution, and unknown-claim evaluation.
why_not_or_caveat: Synthetic enterprise focus; not a method or defense paper.

title: DeepEra: A Deep Evidence Reranking Agent for Scientific Retrieval-Augmented Generated Question Answering
authors: Haotian Chen; Qingqing Long; Siyu Pu; Xiao Luo; Wei Ju; Meng Xiao; Yuanchun Zhou; Jianghua Zhao; Xuezhi Wang
why_relevant: Proposes a reranking agent and benchmark (SciRAG-SSLI) specifically targeting semantically similar but logically irrelevant distractor passages in RAG, directly addressing noisy retrieval and distraction robustness.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on scientific QA domain; reranking-centric rather than full robustness taxonomy.

title: D$^2$Plan: Dual-Agent Dynamic Global Planning for Complex Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning
authors: Kangcheng Luo; Tinglang Wu; Yansong Feng
why_relevant: Proposes a dual-agent planning method to mitigate distraction by irrelevant retrieved evidence and ineffective query construction in multi-hop RAG, with a Purifier explicitly filtering noisy retrievals and adaptive re-retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focus is on multi-hop QA performance rather than systematic robustness analysis or calibration.

title: ConflictRAG: Detecting and Resolving Knowledge Conflicts in Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Chenyu Wang; Yingmin Liu; Yang Shu
why_relevant: Proposes a conflict-aware RAG pipeline that detects, classifies, and resolves inter-document and parametric-contextual conflicts, plus a CARS evaluation metric—directly relevant to the knowledge conflict and evaluation themes.
why_not_or_caveat: Suspicious arXiv ID (2605) suggests possible metadata issue; self-constructed benchmark has acknowledged bias.

title: CAR: Query-Guided Confidence-Aware Reranking for Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Zhipeng Song; Yizhi Zhou; Xiangyu Kong; Jiulong Jiao; Xuezhou Ye; Chunqi Gao; Xueqing Shi; Yuhang Zhou; Heng Qi
suggested_section: Calibration and Control / Filtering Noisy Retrieval
why_relevant: CAR uses generator confidence (semantic consistency of sampled answers) to rerank documents, filtering noisy/unhelpful evidence and gating intervention based on query-level uncertainty—directly addressing calibration-aware control over retrieval and mitigating noisy retrieval in RAG.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on reranking; doesn't address adversarial or conflict cases.

title: AgentSentry: Mitigating Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents via Temporal Causal Diagnostics and Context Purification
authors: Tian Zhang; Yiwei Xu; Juan Wang; Keyan Guo; Xiaoyang Xu; Bowen Xiao; Quanlong Guan; Jinlin Fan; Jiawei Liu; Zhiquan Liu; Hongxin Hu
suggested_section: Adversarial Corruption: Indirect Prompt Injection Defenses
why_relevant: Proposes an inference-time defense against indirect prompt injection in tool/retrieval-augmented LLM agents, directly relevant to adversarial corruption of retrieved content.
why_not_or_caveat: Focuses on agent workflows rather than pure RAG QA; IPI defense via causal diagnostics is agent-centric.

title: Adaptive Guidance for Retrieval-Augmented Masked Diffusion Models
authors: Jaemin Kim; Jong Chul Ye
why_relevant: Proposes adaptive guidance for masked diffusion RAG that dynamically calibrates trust between retrieved context and parametric prior via SNR, directly addressing knowledge conflict and noisy retrieval.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on diffusion language models, a niche substrate compared to autoregressive RAG.

title: A Wolf in Sheep's Clothing: Targeted Routing Hijacking in Federated RAG
authors: Junjie Mu; Qiongxiu Li
why_relevant: Introduces a novel routing-stage attack on Federated RAG where malicious clients forge semantic profiles, causing missing evidence, poisoning, and hallucinations, and proposes a trust-aware defense. Fits adversarial corruption and retrieval robustness themes.
why_not_or_caveat: Focused on federated RAG setting, which is narrower than mainstream RAG robustness.

title: "I Don't Know" -- Towards Appropriate Trust with Certainty-Aware Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Daan Di Scala; Maaike de Boer; Pınar Yolum
why_relevant: Proposes CERTA, a certainty-aware RAG that self-reflects on uncertainty across question-context-answer relevance to enable abstention/hedging, and introduces a benchmark with relevant/incomplete/irrelevant contexts. Directly relevant to calibration, abstention, and noisy retrieval evaluation.
why_not_or_caveat: Small benchmark (90 pairs) focused on non-objective questions; framing emphasizes trust/values more than retrieval robustness per se.
